extracted.intended_audience: Owners, operators, and compliance managers of bulk gasoline terminals; environmental engineers and regulators responsible for VOC control and testing
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and required procedures for controlling, monitoring, testing, and reporting volatile organic compound (VOC/TOC) emissions from gasoline loading racks at bulk gasoline terminals, including design/operation, performance testing, CEMS evaluation, leak detection and repair, and flare/thermal oxidation alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor collection system requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each gasoline loading rack affected facility shall be equipped with a vapor collection system designed and operated to collect the total organic compounds vapors displaced from gasoline cargo tanks during product loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to every gasoline loading rack affected facility. System must be designed and operated to collect displaced vapors during loading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limits — new facility using thermal oxidation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a thermal oxidation system is used, maintain emissions to the atmosphere from the vapor collection system due to loading at or below 1.0 milligram TOC per liter of gasoline loaded (mg/L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continual compliance demonstrated by: (i) initial and periodic performance tests per §60.503a(a)-(c) meeting the emission limitation; and (ii) maintaining combustion zone temperature at or above the 3-hour rolling average operating limit established during the performance test when loading. Valid operating data exclude periods when no liquid product is being loaded (and other exclusions if previous contents known and excluded during limit determination per §60.503a(c)(8)(ii)). Flares cannot be used to comply with this limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limits — new facility using vapor recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: If a vapor recovery system is used, maintain emissions to the atmosphere from the vapor collection system at or below 550 ppmv of TOC as propane determined on a 3-hour rolling average when the vapor recovery system is operating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate the vapor recovery system during all periods when capable of processing gasoline vapors (including loading, carbon bed regeneration, bed preparation). Operate to minimize air/nitrogen intrusion except as needed for designed operation. Use of gaseous diluents to achieve concentration-based standards is prohibited (consistent with §60.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limits — modified/reconstructed facility using thermal oxidation
rubrics_metrics.description: For modified or reconstructed facilities using a thermal oxidation system, maintain emissions at or below 10 mg/L TOC due to loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate continual compliance by: (i) conducting initial and periodic performance tests per §60.503a(a)-(c); (ii) maintaining combustion zone temperature at or above the 3-hour rolling average operating limit established during the performance test when loading (with valid data exclusions as specified); or (iii) electing the alternative monitoring provisions specified in paragraph (c)(3) of the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission limits — modified/reconstructed facility using vapor recovery
rubrics_metrics.description: For modified or reconstructed facilities using a vapor recovery system, maintain emissions at or below 5,500 ppmv of TOC as propane determined on a 3-hour rolling average when the vapor recovery system is operating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operate the vapor recovery system whenever capable of processing vapors (including loading and carbon bed regeneration) and minimize air/nitrogen intrusion except as needed for designed operation. Use of gaseous diluents to meet concentration standards is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare / thermal oxidation alternative monitoring provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a flare is used or thermal oxidation system elects the monitoring alternative, meet applicable requirements in §63.670(b)-(g) and (i)-(n) of this chapter except as modified by specific substitutions and provisions in paragraphs (c)(3)(i)–(ix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes multiple specific substitutions (e.g., definitions of regulated materials, visible emissions monitoring substitution, flare tip velocity exceptions, terminology substitutions) and allows alternative approaches for determining flare vent flow rate by cumulative liquid loading rates, with further monitoring and application requirements described in paragraphs (c)(3)(i)–(ix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assume previous cargo contents when unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: If you do not know the previous contents of the cargo tank, you must assume that cargo tank is a gasoline cargo tank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption applies when applying provisions that depend on previous tank contents (e.g., when determining regulated materials for flare provisions and other monitoring/operational requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible emissions monitoring substitution for flares
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitute 'The owner or operator shall monitor for visible emissions from the flare as specified in §60.504a(c)(4).' for the paragraph referenced in §63.670(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific substitution replacing referenced language in §63.670 for purposes of this subpart; follow §60.504a(c)(4) for visible emissions monitoring requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare tip velocity and related exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain phrases in §63.670(d) and related provisions for flare tip velocity do not apply; alternative one-time flare tip velocity compliance assessment may be elected as specified in (c)(3)(ix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-time assessment requires: (A) determine unobstructed flare tip area per §63.670(k)(1); (B) determine maximum flow rate based on maximum cumulative 15-minute loading considering restrictions in paragraph (h); (C) calculate max flare tip velocity = max flow / tip area; (D) demonstrate max velocity is < 60 feet/second. Repeat assessment if flare/loading rack configuration changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining flare vent gas flow rate alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: As an alternative to flow rate monitoring alternatives in §63.670(i), you may determine flare waste gas flow rate by monitoring cumulative loading rates of all liquid products loaded into cargo tanks whose displaced vapors are managed by the facility's vapor collection and processing systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cumulative loading rates for 15-minute block periods across all loading racks directed to the flare/processing system; consider maximum loading restrictions necessary for compliance with maximum pressure limits in paragraph (h).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flare gas composition monitoring and exemption application
rubrics_metrics.description: If using §63.670(j)(6) for flare vent gas composition monitoring and seeking an exemption from monitoring, submit a separate written application to the Administrator and determine and document specific gasoline-to-total-liquid ratios and minimum gasoline loading rates as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requirements to (A) submit written application for exemption; (B) determine minimum gasoline/total liquid ratio and minimum gasoline loading rate (15-minute period) to ensure lowest net heating value conditions; (C) collect samples under identified conditions; (D) treat seasonal gasoline changes as changes in operating conditions; (E) monitor volumes on a 5-minute block basis and maintain ratios and rolling 15-minute gasoline loading rates; and (F)/(G) relate net heating value thresholds to demonstration of compliance with NHVcz and NHVdil operating limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to establish and monitor supplemental gas addition rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners/operators may elect to establish a minimum supplemental gas addition rate and monitor it to demonstrate compliance with flare combustion zone operating limits and, if applicable, dilution operating limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: (A) use minimum flare vent gas net heating value prior to supplemental gas; (B) determine maximum flow rate based on max cumulative 15-minute loading and pressure restrictions; (C) compute supplemental rate to reach NHVcz 270 Btu/scf using §63.670(m)(1); (D) for perimeter assist systems compute rate to reach NHVdil 22 Btu/ft2 using §63.670(n)(1) across air assist settings and choose max supplemental rate; (E) maintain supplemental rate above the greater of determined values on a 15-minute block basis when loading for at least 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor collection system design between racks
rubrics_metrics.description: Each vapor collection system for the gasoline loading rack affected facility shall be designed to prevent any TOC vapors collected at one loading rack from passing to another loading rack.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design requirement to keep collected vapors segregated by rack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor-tight cargo tank requirement and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Loadings into gasoline cargo tanks shall be limited to vapor-tight gasoline cargo tanks demonstrated within the prior 12 months to meet the annual certification test requirements in §60.503a(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner/operator must obtain vapor tightness annual certification test documentation per §60.505a(a)(3) for each tank to be loaded. If previous contents unknown, assume tank is gasoline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cargo tank identification and cross-checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner/operator shall obtain and record the cargo tank identification number of each gasoline cargo tank to be loaded and cross-check that ID with the file of vapor tightness documentation prior to loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check required before loading any liquid product into the gasoline cargo tank; treat unknown previous contents as gasoline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submerged filling and compatible vapor collection equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Loading of liquid product into gasoline cargo tanks shall be conducted using submerged filling and only into tanks equipped with vapor collection equipment compatible with the terminal's vapor collection system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submerged filling is defined in §60.501a. If previous tank contents unknown, assume gasoline cargo tank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vapor systems must be connected during loading
rubrics_metrics.description: Loading shall only be conducted when the terminal's and the cargo tank's vapor collection systems are connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If previous contents unknown, assume gasoline cargo tank and ensure connection before loading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cargo tank gauge pressure limit and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Vapor collection and liquid loading equipment shall be designed and operated to prevent gauge pressure in the cargo tank from exceeding 18 inches of water (460 mm) during product loading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This level must not be exceeded and must be continuously monitored per procedures in §60.504a(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure-vacuum vent setpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: No pressure-vacuum vent in the vapor collection system shall begin to open at a system pressure less than 18 inches of water or at a vacuum of less than 6.0 inches of water (150 mm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design/operation requirement for vent setpoints to prevent premature opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak inspection and repair program — scope and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Each owner/operator shall perform leak inspection and repair of all equipment in gasoline service (vapor collection system, vapor processing system, each loading rack and loading arm) and keep a list, summary description, or diagram(s) showing locations of all equipment in gasoline service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program applies to the entire set of equipment in gasoline service at the facility; maintain documentation of equipment locations and descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak detection monitoring methods and frequencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct leak detection monitoring of all pumps, valves, and connectors in gasoline service using either: (i) optical gas imaging (OGI) quarterly per §60.503a(e)(2), or (ii) Method 21 of appendix A-7 with specified monitoring frequencies and leak definitions in §60.503a(e)(1) and paragraphs (j)(1)(ii)(A)-(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method 21 specifics: pumps monitored quarterly (unless exempted), valves quarterly (unless exempted), connectors annually (unless exempted). An instrument reading of 10,000 ppm or greater is a leak for Method 21 monitoring unless a different threshold specified elsewhere. Use OGI per appendix K if that option is selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-sensitivity monitoring before performance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately before the performance test, conduct leak detection monitoring using the methods in paragraph (e)(1) to identify leakage from all equipment (including loading arms) while gasoline is being loaded, to ensure equipment is operated with no detectable emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repair all leaks identified with readings of 500 ppmv (as methane) or greater above background before conducting the performance test and within timeframes specified in §60.502a(j)(7). For this pre-test monitoring the instrument calibration gas must be at 500 ppm methane (see paragraph (e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording leaks detected during normal duties
rubrics_metrics.description: During normal duties, record leaks identified by audio, visual, or olfactory methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records of such detections are required as part of the leak detection program; these detections constitute evidence of a leak per paragraph (j)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Any evidence of potential leak constitutes a leak
rubrics_metrics.description: If evidence of a potential leak is found at any time by audio, visual, olfactory, or any other detection method for any equipment, a leak is detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers repair procedures and the marking/tagging/repair timeline obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pressure relief device monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct instrument monitoring of each pressure relief device quarterly and within 5 calendar days after each pressure release to detect leaks using the methods in paragraph (j)(1), except as provided in §60.482-4a(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If emissions observed using OGI, a leak is detected. If Method 21 is used, instrument reading of 10,000 ppm or greater indicates a leak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special equipment categories — sampling connections and open-ended lines
rubrics_metrics.description: For sampling connection systems, comply with §60.482-5a; for open-ended valves or lines, comply with §60.482-6a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow referenced sections for specific monitoring and control requirements for these equipment types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leak identification tagging and repair timing
rubrics_metrics.description: When a leak is detected, attach a weatherproof visible identification marked with the equipment ID; initial attempt at repair shall be made as soon as practicable but no later than 5 calendar days after detection (with specific exception for OGI and elevated work), and repair or replacement must be completed within 15 calendar days unless delay provisions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification may be removed after repair. For instrument-identified leaks, repair confirmed by re-monitoring showing no leak; for audio/visual/olfactory-identified leaks, repair confirmed when leak can no longer be identified by those methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay of repair — allowed circumstances and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay of repair is allowed under specified conditions (equipment isolated and not in gasoline service; purged-material emission considerations for valves/connectors; valve assembly replacement supply depletion up to 3 months; pump repairs requiring dual mechanical seal systems may be delayed up to 6 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner/operator must provide reasons for delayed repair and completion dates in the semiannual report per §60.505a(c). For valve/connectors delay due to purged material, owner/operator must demonstrate that purging emissions exceed immediate-repair fugitive emissions and collect/destroy or recover purged material in approved control devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measures to prevent extended vapor releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities must not handle gasoline in ways that would result in vapor releases to the atmosphere for extended periods; required measures include minimizing spills, cleaning up spills expeditiously, covering open gasoline containers and storage tank fill-pipes with gasketed seals when not in use, and minimizing gasoline sent to open waste collection systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are illustrative but required measures to avoid extended vapor releases; use reclamation/recycling devices (e.g., oil/water separators) when handling collected gasoline.

rubrics_metrics.name: General test method use and pre-test leak repair
rubrics_metrics.description: In conducting required performance tests/evaluations, use the test methods and procedures specified in §60.503a (except as provided in §60.8(b)). Immediately before a performance test, conduct leak detection (per (e)(1)) and repair leaks ≥500 ppm methane above background before testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-run requirement of §60.8(f) does not apply to this subpart. Follow referenced methods and procedures exactly unless an alternative is approved under §60.8(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test/evaluation timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial performance tests or evaluations follow timing in §60.8(a). Subsequent tests: for mass emission limits (§60.502a(b)(1) or (c)(1)) conduct subsequent performance test no later than 60 calendar months after previous test; for concentration emission limits (§60.502a(b)(2) or (c)(2)) conduct subsequent performance evaluations of CEMS no later than 12 months after previous evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the specified schedules for retesting and annual/subsequent evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance test duration and gasoline throughput requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance test for mass loading emission limit shall be 6 hours long during which at least 80,000 gallons (300,000 liters) of gasoline is loaded. If not possible, test may continue same day until 80,000 gallons loaded, or resume next day with another 6-hour period (the 80,000-gallon criterion need not be met during second-day testing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing should be conducted during the 6-hour period with the highest normal throughput as much as possible. If the vapor processor is intermittent with an intermediate vapor holder, testing should begin and end at the same reference vapor holder level and include at least two startups and shutdowns of the vapor processor (manual control if automatic does not provide two cycles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission rate computation and 5-minute intervals
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute emission rate (E, mg/L gasoline) using the specified equation with 5-minute testing intervals: record readings each interval, determine exhausted volume Vesi and average TOC concentration Cei for each interval, and account for sampling system response time when matching concentration to exhausted volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use K = density of calibration gas (1.83 × 10^6 for propane, mg/scm), n = number of intervals, i = 5-minute intervals. Method 2B for volume determination and Method 25/25A/25B for TOC concentration are specified elsewhere in the section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volume determination method for performance test
rubrics_metrics.description: Method 2B of appendix A-1 must be used to determine the volume (Vesi) of air-vapor mixture exhausted at each interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Method 2B procedures for accurate exhausted volume measurement during each 5-minute interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: TOC concentration measurement and methane exclusion procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Method 25, 25A, or 25B of appendix A-7 must be used for TOC concentration (Cei) measurements. Method 25 must not be used if outlet TOC < 50 ppmv. Calibration gas must be propane. If using 25A or 25B, methane in the exhaust may be excluded following specified procedures (measure methane by Method 18 or Method 320, calibrate analyzer to propane and methane to get response factors, determine TOC as methane basis, subtract methane, convert difference to TOC as propane) or use GC-FID with heated lines to directly measure TOC minus methane per paragraph (c)(6)(vi).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using GC-FID, separate methane and measure, back-flush column; sampling components heated >110°C; calibrate with propane; record TOC minus methane at least once every 15 minutes; include calibration and separation demonstration in performance test report. Follow detailed stepwise procedures (i)-(vi) for methane subtraction and conversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine gasoline volume dispensed during test
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine L (volume of gasoline dispensed during performance test), use terminal records or readings from gasoline dispensing meters at each loading rack whose vapors are controlled by the processing system being tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accurate terminal records or meter readings for all loading racks under the control of the tested processing system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combustion zone temperature monitoring and operating limit determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor combustion zone temperature using the continuous parameter monitoring system (CPMS) required in §60.504a(a) and determine the operating limit by recording temperature (or average) for each 5-minute period, calculating 1-hour averages using only periods when liquid product is loaded, computing 3-hour rolling averages starting at end of third hour, and setting the operating limit at the lowest 3-hour average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a 6-hour test this yields four 3-hour averages. New operating limits become effective on the date the performance test report is submitted to EPA CEDRI per §60.505a(b). If previous cargo contents unknown, assume product loading into gasoline cargo tanks and include all 5-minute loading periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: CEMS performance evaluation specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: For CEMS used with concentration emission limits: (1) nondispersive infrared analyzers must be installed/evaluated/operated per Performance Specification 8 (appendix B), with Method 25B as the reference method and propane calibration gas; (2) flame ionization detector (FID) CEMS must meet Performance Specification 8A, include a RATA per Performance Specification 2 (section 8.4), meet relative accuracy criteria of Performance Specification 8 (section 13.2), and use Method 25A as the reference with propane calibration gas. Methane exclusion procedures are allowed per paragraphs (d)(2)(i)-(iv).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may request alternative test method under §60.8(b) to use a CEMS that excludes methane. If TOC minus methane > 50 ppmv, Method 25 must be used as reference; if ≤ 50 ppmv, Method 25A is to be used. Record TOC minus methane at least once every 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method 21 leak detection calibration and drift procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When using Method 21: leak definition is instrument reading of 10,000 ppmv (as methane). Instrument must be calibrated before each day of use using zero air (<10 ppm hydrocarbon) and methane/air at 10,000 ppm methane. At end of each monitoring day perform drift assessment; if negative drift >10% re-monitor equipment as specified; positive drift >10% allows owner/operator discretion for re-monitoring specified equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Method 21 calibration and drift assessment procedures; if multiple scales used record readings for each scale. Re-monitoring thresholds and arithmetic calculations for drift are specified in paragraph (e)(1)(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: OGI leak detection option
rubrics_metrics.description: Optical gas imaging (OGI) may be used to quarterly monitor all pumps, valves, and connectors in gasoline service according to all requirements in appendix K to this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OGI is an alternative to Method 21 with its own requirements; note special exceptions for repair timing if OGI-identified leaks require elevated access >2 m.
